source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

We were impressed with your test submission and would be delighted to bring you on board to update our Leadership Interview Questions You'll Most Likely Be Asked book!

To ensure we are aligned from the outset, we’d like to explain the project’s complete scope so you know exactly what the work will involve.

**Project Aim**

Our goal is to revise the first edition of the Leadership Interview Questions book so that it aligns with present-day industry standards and remains useful to current readers. The book is a quick-reference interview preparation guide for managers, team leads, and senior professionals who have 4 to 5+ years of experience, as well as people entering leadership positions for the first time. We also want to incorporate a global viewpoint by illustrating how interview questions and answers may differ across countries and industries.

**Project Stages**

**1. Reviewing and updating existing content (Milestone 1)**
We’ll provide the first edition for your review. While examining the 250 questions, we’d like your recommendations on which questions should be removed because they are outdated, no longer align with the modern leadership environment, or duplicate other questions in the book.

--Refining the full question set according to your review

--Writing answers for the content that remains. Please keep in mind that the answer layers previously discussed—interviewer’s intent, common mistakes, how to structure the answer, and answer framework—might not be suitable for every question. After we jointly finalize the question set, we can identify which questions require every layer and which only need a couple.

**2. Adding new chapters (Milestone 2)**
We would like to add several new sections/chapters and welcome your input on how best to shape them:

--A pre-interview preparation checklist. Because the intended readers already have professional experience, this section may benefit from focusing on leadership-specific preparation instead of basic advice. We’d like to include any tips that are particularly applicable to leadership-level interviews.

--Remote & Hybrid Leadership questions

--Questions candidates can ask the interviewer

--How to use AI for interview preparation (prompts, techniques, tools)

--Questions created specifically for first-time leaders

In your response to the previous briefing, you identified the chapters you considered most relevant, which was helpful. However, unless a chapter contains question & answer content, we expect all chapters to remain short. The AI chapter appears to offer readers the most distinctive benefit. Given the current environment, knowing how to apply AI to different tasks is important, so that chapter must be included.

**3. Hybrid Experience (Milestone 3)**

--Our books are intended to provide a hybrid learning experience because some readers prefer not to go through a book cover-to-cover. In addition to the book itself, we want to provide online companion materials such as checklists, AI prompts, body-language videos, mock interviews, answer templates, leadership resume tips, and any other resources you might recommend.

**A Note on Word Count**

While reviewing the existing content and preparing additions, please monitor the book’s total word count. Our limit is 50K words, while the first edition contains approximately 37K, which initially leaves about 13K words available. However, because the revision will be extensive and some questions will be removed, we expect that additional space may become available. The completed book must not exceed 50K words overall.

We have also included our author guidelines for the Interview series. Please review them and tell us if any part requires further explanation. Link to author guidelines: [URL_002]

Here is also the complete book in Google Doc format. We’re working in Google Doc so changes can be tracked, although we can provide a PDF as a reference if that is more convenient: [URL_003]

After the project starts, we will provide the actual working manuscript and make the appropriate changes.

We’re looking forward to collaborating with you on this, [FREELANCER_NAME_001]. Please reach out if you have any questions. If a call would help address your concerns, we can arrange one.

source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you for your patience while we prepare the contract. To keep our internal process organized, we will wait until the contract is finalized before providing an editable or downloadable version of the document. After the terms have been agreed upon, we’ll send you the PDF so you can begin working in advance.

We would like to restate the work scope we intend to put into the contract:

**1. Addition of chapters (5, as discussed earlier)**

A. Basic chapters (these are not question & answers and should be 2.5k - 3.5k words or less)

--Pre-interview preparation checklist. Since the readers already have experience, this should take a leadership-specific approach rather than covering only fundamentals. We would like to include preparation advice that is particularly relevant to leadership-level interviews.

--How to use AI for interview preparation (prompts, techniques, tools)

B. Question & Answers chapters (The author may include as many questions as they consider appropriate in each chapter, provided they account for the book’s total word count.)

--Questions candidates can ask the interviewer

--Questions intended specifically for first-time leaders

--Remote & Hybrid Leadership questions

**2. Reviewing the existing content and updating it (As agreed during the previous discussions, you will review and revise the content according to the provided directions.)**

--Refining the question set in every chapter (category) contained in the current edition, or across the 250 questions. To produce the strongest possible content, the author may recommend any of the following options:

1. Eliminate a category or combine two categories (chapters).

2. Delete individual questions after explaining the rationale.

3. Introduce new questions within a category so the new edition reflects questions being asked in today’s workplace.

4. Create a new question category if it is not already represented.

5. Recommend improved wording for any questions the author believes could be rephrased and used more effectively.

--Writing answers and supplying answers for newly added questions (as agreed: 2 mandatory and 2 subjective)

1. Mandatory answer layers: How to frame the answers, with answer frameworks incorporated here, and a sample answer.

2. Subjective answer layers: Interviewer’s intent & common mistakes

Any proposed addition or removal of a category/chapter or question must be properly reviewed by the editorial team before it can be implemented. As previously agreed, the author will examine the complete book—all 250 questions—and provide feedback to the team during the first milestone.

**3. Hybrid resources**

--Because readers do not all prefer to finish books cover-to-cover, we aim to provide a hybrid learning experience with every title. In addition to the book, we want to supply online companion resources such as checklists, AI prompts, body-language videos, mock interviews, answer templates, leadership resume tips, and any other materials you recommend.

The completed book should have an overall word count of 50k. The author must therefore plan the material around that limit and remain within it.

The author may propose other revisions or additions that could make the book more interactive and relevant for today’s readers. Those ideas will only be implemented after consultation with the editorial team.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Please confirm that these project requirements are clear and that you are comfortable proceeding.

Our team is completing the contract and will provide it to you shortly for review.

Thank you for waiting! We are eager to collaborate with you and begin this project as soon as we can.

routing_warnings.description: The requirement to delete proposed removals in suggesting mode and leave a rationale comment is a tracked-editing and documentation obligation rather than a change to the curation criteria.
The clauses about introducing new questions, creating a new category, and improving question wording concern content modernization rather than selection and organization of the existing inventory.
The requirement for editorial review before implementing proposed additions or removals belongs to the independent editorial-approval Requirement.
The instruction to make actual edits in the Google Doc using suggestion mode and comments concerns the tracked manuscript-editing workflow.
